name: Rune
works_with: Rust apps on macOS, Windows, Linux and the web
short: A GPU-rendered Rust UI framework for desktop and web that your coding agent can test headlessly by rendering PNGs.
what: Rune is a native Rust UI framework with its own renderer, text, layout and spring animations. It runs on macOS, Windows, Linux and the web. Every app can also run headless, so an agent can render screens to PNG, dump the element tree and drive the app with scripted input.
who: Rust developers building desktop or web apps, especially with a coding agent doing the work. It is pre-release, so skip it if you need a stable API.
needs: A coding agent if you want to follow the README's workflow

steps.title: Add it to Cargo.toml
steps.text: Replace `<dev rev>` with a commit from the `dev` branch. Pin a rev, because Rune is pre-release. The `dev` branch is never rewritten.

steps.title: Hand it to your agent
steps.text: Point your agent at `examples/hello` and `crates/rune/README.md`, and have it check its own work by rendering PNGs and inspecting the element tree.

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Build me a <thing> with Rune (github.com/anomalyco/rune). Start from examples/hello and check your work headlessly."

watch: The project takes no pull requests. You report bugs and ideas as GitHub issues.
The README does not list system requirements.
